note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment planning following stable ISUP grade group 1 prostate cancer with high-risk histological features on repeat biopsy.

The patient is an 82-year-old semi-retired harbour pilot living alone, with his adult daughter managing communications and medical correspondence. He has a history of hypertension, coronary artery disease, and osteoarthritis, managed with valsartan, lisinopril, atorvastatin, metoprolol, and paracetamol. He maintains an active lifestyle, running 5 km three times weekly, and consumes 8 units of alcohol per week. Recent appointments include a pain clinic visit for chronic shoulder pain and a sleep clinic evaluation for suspected obstructive sleep apnoea. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 5/35. There is no history of haematuria, bone pain, or unexplained weight loss. His PSA has risen steadily from 1.4 ng/mL in March 2023 to 4.7 ng/mL in January 2025.

Digital rectal examination reveals a smooth, symmetrically enlarged prostate without discrete nodules or asymmetry, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination shows a well-nourished patient with stable vital signs and no signs of lymphadenopathy or bone tenderness.
